wars.name: Allied assault on Mérida
wars.outcome: The Kuchkabal page has Cupul, Cochuah and Sotuta in 'their allied assault on Spanish forces at Mérida in 1542'; the outcome is not stated.
wars.note: The Cochuah page has a Dávila entrada 'to this province in 1531' with no outcome.

sources.title: Kuchkabal
sources.note: Provinces of Yucatan with capitals; 1542 allied assault on Mérida (Cupul, Cochuah, Sotuta); 1545 Nachi Cocom; 1557 Mani treaty; extents debated.

sources.title: Spanish conquest of Yucatán
sources.note: Province neighbours; Montejo 1527; Campeche 1531; retreat 1534/35; Campeche and Mérida councils 1541-42; late 1546 uprising of eastern provinces.

sources.title: Mayapan
sources.note: Xiu revolt 1441; Cocom killed; 'Yucatan devolved into warring city-states'.

sources.title: Cochuah
sources.note: Capital Tihosuco (or Chunhuhub); Dávila entrada 1531; borders Cupul north, Sotuta, Tutul Xiu and Chakan Putun west; forests to the Bay of Ascension.

notes: NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no row for this province; Later Mayan City-States (1429-1546, 135,136 to 187,745 km2) covers the whole northern lowlands and contains it. The Kuchkabal page says the extent of the provinces 'is still debated' and that scholars disagree 'on whether they were territorial units or jurisdictions'; the shape here is a disc around the capital, soft, and no frontier is claimed. Cliopatria keeps its envelope to 1546 although the Spanish took the provinces one by one from 1527. COCHUAH. The page: ruler 'Nakahum Cochuah' resided at Tihosuco in 1579 (after the end). Gazetteer lacks 'Tihosuco'.
